blocks.text: Every megawatt that leaves Kainji, Shiroro or Egbin starts the same way: a coil of copper is spun in a magnetic field until an e.m.f. is induced. The same physics lights a bicycle dynamo on a dusty road in Kano. Move a conductor across field lines — or change the field through a coil — and a voltage appears.

blocks.markdown:
**Electromagnetic induction** is the production of an e.m.f. whenever the magnetic flux linking a circuit changes. Magnetic flux through an area $A$ is $\Phi = BA\cos\theta$; **flux linkage** of a coil is $N\Phi$.

**Faraday's laws**

1. Whenever the magnetic flux linking a circuit changes, an e.m.f. is induced in the circuit.
2. The magnitude of the induced e.m.f. is proportional to the rate of change of flux linkage:

$$E = -N\frac{\Delta\Phi}{\Delta t}$$

**Lenz's law** fixes the sign: the induced current flows in the direction that **opposes** the change causing it. That is why there is a minus sign. Push a north pole into a coil and the induced current makes the near end a north pole, which repels your magnet — you have to do work, and that work becomes electrical energy.

blocks.title: What Lenz's law is protecting
blocks.text: If the induced current aided the change, you would get energy for nothing and conservation of energy would fail. Opposition is not a nuisance — it is the law of conservation of energy written in magnetic language.

items: Number of turns N: more loops, more flux linkage, larger E.
Strength of the field B: stronger magnet or larger current in an electromagnet.
Area of the coil A: a bigger face intercepts more flux.
Speed of the change: move the magnet faster, spin the coil faster, or switch the field off more quickly — ΔΦ/Δt rises, so E rises.
For a straight rod of length l moving at speed v perpendicular to B, E = Blv.

blocks.title: Induced e.m.f. in a moving rod
blocks.prompt: A metal rod of length 0.20 m slides at 4.0 m/s on conducting rails, perpendicular to a uniform field of 0.50 T. Calculate the induced e.m.f.

steps.text: The rod, the velocity and the field are mutually perpendicular, so the motional-e.m.f. formula applies.
Substitute the values in SI units.
If the rod moved parallel to B there would be no cutting of flux and E would be zero.

blocks.markdown:
### The simple a.c. generator

A coil is rotated at a steady angular speed in a uniform magnetic field. The flux through the coil varies as $\Phi = BA\cos\omega t$, so the induced e.m.f. is sinusoidal:

$$E = NBA\omega\sin\omega t$$

- $E$ is **zero** when the coil face is perpendicular to $B$ (flux a maximum, but not changing).
- $E$ is a **maximum** when the coil is parallel to $B$ (flux zero, but changing at its fastest).

**Slip rings** and carbon brushes take the alternating current out to the external circuit: the same brush always sits on the same side of the coil, so the output reverses every half-turn — true a.c.

A **split-ring commutator** (two half-rings) reverses the coil-to-brush connections every half-turn, so the external current is always in one direction — a **d.c. dynamo**. That is the only essential difference between the a.c. generator and the d.c. generator at this level.

rows: When E in the coil is a maximum
blocks.caption: Same rotating coil, different method of taking the current off. Fleming's right-hand rule (thumb = Motion, first finger = Field, second = induced Current) gives the direction in the wire.

blocks.title: WAEC and JAMB tip
blocks.text: Maximum flux is not maximum e.m.f. Faraday's law cares about the rate of change of flux, not the flux itself. Sketch E against time as a sine wave starting from zero if the coil starts face-on to the field. And never credit a split ring with producing a.c. — that is the whole point of the commutator.

points: Faraday: an e.m.f. is induced whenever flux linkage changes, and E = −N ΔΦ/Δt.
Lenz: the induced current opposes the change that produces it, so energy is conserved.
Induced e.m.f. is larger for more turns, a stronger field, a larger area and a faster change; for a rod, E = Blv.
An a.c. generator uses slip rings; a d.c. dynamo uses a split-ring commutator.
The coil e.m.f. is a maximum when the coil is parallel to the field (flux changing fastest) and zero when the coil is perpendicular to the field.
